title: Two-term perfect models, Tor amplitude, and preservation by pullback
statement: For every scheme X [def-pc-scheme] with the recorded derived categories on X and its localized sites [def-pc-derived-category], the local two-term finite locally free condition [def-trf-two-term-determinant-data] is equivalent to being perfect [def-pc-perfect-complex] with derived tensor cohomology vanishing outside [-1,0] [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Every displayed model and the zero complex satisfy the condition, and arbitrary derived pullback preserves it [def-pc-module-pullback]. No quasi-compactness, separatedness or uniform global rank hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Trivialize the two model terms on a common open refinement. The mapped complex has finite free terms and support [-1,0]. It is strictly perfect. Bounded-above flat K-flatness and the termwise tensor calculation give the required cohomology vanishings.

Use perfectness and Tor-amplitude locality on open neighbourhoods to descend these properties. Open pullback is exact restriction, with the universe-polymorphic comparison lifted through localization.

At a point choose the finite free residue model. Its ranks are the residue Betti numbers. The assumed tensor vanishings make all ranks outside [-1,0] zero. The corresponding terms vanish; compare the complex to the double of its remaining differential componentwise.

For a model use its locally free trivializations; for zero use a finite free complex all of whose terms vanish. For arbitrary pullback, pull the residue model to the inverse-image open using localizedPullback. It preserves finite free terms and zero objects; the retained strictly-perfect-model comparison identifies this with derived pullback.

mathlib_searches.query: determinant functor two term perfect complexes invertible sheaf pullback
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits about free module pullback isomorphisms; none constructs determinant functors or affine descent. For the Tor-window search, DerivedCategory.exists_iso_Q_obj_of_isGE_of_isLE gives a cohomologically bounded complex, without finite locally free terms. The existing finite-free residue model in our library supplies the stronger input.
Zero hits. The separate "Perfect", "Tor" query returned unrelated perfect groups, perfect closures and graph matchings.

Two hits in Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Complex/Determinant.lean concern complex numbers, not complexes. The additional leftAdjointCompIso search found the mate/composition API used in the proved normalized-coherence argument. No determinant construction was found.

mathlib_searches.query: Determinant line of two term perfect complexes compatible with affine base change and descent
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits: LinearMap.det, IsBaseChange.det_endHom, LinearEquiv.det_baseChange, LinearMap.det_baseChange and related scalar determinants. These are endomorphism determinants, not determinant lines of complexes or compatible gluing data. The queried theorem types do not provide the required construction.

lean.statement:
theorem isTwoTermPerfect_iff_perfect_tor
    [∀ (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens),
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (L : schemeDerivedCategory X) :
    isTwoTermPerfect X L ↔ Scheme.IsPerfect X L ∧
      ∀ (M : SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) (i : ℤ),
        i < -1 ∨ 0 < i → IsZero ((DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor _ i).obj
          (L ⊗ (DerivedCategory.singleFunctor _ 0).obj M))
